_meta: Circuit library texts. Beta languages (fr, pl, pt-BR, tr, nl) fall back to English per key.
not_gate.name: NOT gate (inverter)
not_gate.desc: The lever powers the block, and a redstone torch on the side of a powered block turns off. So the lamp is on while the input is off – and the other way round. The building block for almost every other gate.
or_gate.name: OR gate
or_gate.desc: Both inputs simply join the same redstone line: if either lever is on, the lamp lights up. Use it to control one door or lamp from several places.
and_gate.name: AND gate
and_gate.desc: Each input switches off the torch on top of its block. Only when both torches are off does the line between them go dark, and the output torch on the middle block lights up. Needs both inputs – for example two buttons for a vault.
xor_gate.name: XOR gate
xor_gate.desc: Two comparators in subtract mode: each gets its own input from behind and the other input from the side. With exactly one input on, one comparator outputs; with both on, both subtract to 0. The classic for a light you switch from two places.
repeater_chain.name: Repeater chain
repeater_chain.desc: Redstone dust loses one signal level per block, so after 15 blocks the signal is gone. A repeater refreshes it back to 15. For long lines, put a repeater at least every 15 blocks – each one adds a small delay.
torch_tower.name: Signal upwards (torch tower)
torch_tower.desc: Blocks and redstone torches stacked alternately: each torch powers the block above it and inverts the signal. With an even number of torches the top gets the same signal as the bottom. A compact way to send a signal straight up.
observer_clock.name: Observer clock
observer_clock.desc: Two observers watching each other: when one pulses, the other sees the change and pulses back. This is the fastest simple clock. It starts when the second observer is placed; break one to stop it. Great for flying machines and farms.
observer_clock.note: Very fast clocks may be slowed down or removed by anti-lag plugins on some servers.
repeater_clock.name: Repeater clock
repeater_clock.desc: Four repeaters in a loop: a short pulse from the button runs around the ring forever. Its speed is the sum of all repeater delays (here 4 × 4 ticks ≈ 1.6 s per round). To stop it, break a piece of dust for a moment.
comparator_clock.name: Comparator clock
comparator_clock.desc: A comparator in subtract mode feeds its own output back into its side. The output keeps subtracting itself away, so it flickers very fast as long as the lever is on. Tiny and easy to switch on and off.
comparator_clock.note: Very fast – some anti-lag plugins limit clocks like this.
rs_latch.name: RS latch (memory cell)
rs_latch.desc: Two torches that keep each other in check: S (set) switches the output on, R (reset) switches it off, and the state stays when the lever goes back. Remembers one bit – for example “is the farm running?”.
t_flipflop.name: T flip-flop (repeater locks)
t_flipflop.desc: Every button press toggles the lamp. Two repeaters work as a memory pair: while the button is held, the first takes the inverted output; when it is released, the second copies it. Works in every version from 1.8 – no pistons, no quasi-connectivity.
t_flipflop_copper.name: T flip-flop (copper bulb)
t_flipflop_copper.desc: A copper bulb toggles its light with every new signal. A comparator reads the bulb and outputs 15 while it is lit. The easiest toggle from Minecraft 1.21 on – wax the bulb so it does not oxidize.
d_latch.name: D latch
d_latch.desc: While E (enable) is on, the output follows D. When E is off, a torch locks the data repeater from the side and the output keeps its last value. Stores a value at exactly the moment you choose.
monoflop.name: Monoflop (short pulse on switch-on)
monoflop.desc: The input reaches the comparator at once from behind and a little later from the side through a repeater. In subtract mode the output is only on in between – one short pulse, however long the lever stays on. Set the length with the repeater delay.
edge_observer.name: Edge detector (observer)
edge_observer.desc: An observer watches the redstone line: it notices every change and gives a short pulse – when the lever is switched on and again when it is switched off. Needs Minecraft 1.11 or newer.
falling_edge.name: Falling-edge detector
falling_edge.desc: Like the monoflop the other way round: the comparator gets the delayed signal from behind and the fast one from the side. Only when the input switches off is the side already empty while the back is still on – that makes one short pulse.
pulse_extender.name: Pulse extender
pulse_extender.desc: The button signal goes straight to the output and, in parallel, through two slow repeaters. The output stays on until the delayed copy is over too – a 1 s press becomes about 1.8 s. Add repeaters for longer pulses. The repeater in the direct path stops the signal from running backwards.
piston_door_2x2.name: 2×2 piston door
piston_door_2x2.desc: Four sticky pistons hold the door blocks in the opening. Torches keep them powered; a pressure plate powers the line under the floor, the torches go out and the pistons pull the blocks into the walls. Build walls around the pistons and hide the dust under the floor.
hidden_stairs.name: Hidden staircase (simple)
hidden_stairs.desc: Three sticky pistons with redstone dust on top form a staircase of dust. Flip the lever and every piston pushes its step one block out of the wall; flip it back and the steps disappear into the wall. Build the wall flush with the step blocks.
sugarcane_observer.name: Sugar cane farm cell
sugarcane_observer.desc: An observer watches the spot where the second sugar cane block grows. As soon as it appears, the observer pulses and a piston breaks it; the bottom block keeps growing. Put hoppers or a water stream below to collect the drops and line up many cells side by side.
item_filter.name: Item filter (sorter cell)
item_filter.desc: The filter hopper holds 18 of the item to sort in its first slot and one renamed placeholder item in each other slot. That gives comparator strength 1 – not enough to reach the repeater. A 19th matching item makes it 2: the torch goes out, the lower hopper unlocks, pulls one item into the chest and locks again. Other items travel on along the hopper line on top.
item_filter.note: Some servers (Paper/Spigot) change hopper timing; the filter usually still works, but test it in your world first.
auto_smelter.name: Automatic furnace
auto_smelter.desc: Items from the top chest drop into the furnace from above, fuel comes in from the side, and the smelted results fall out below into a chest. No redstone needed – the classic basis for bigger furnace arrays.
item_elevator.name: Item elevator (bubble column)
item_elevator.desc: Soul sand under water sources makes a bubble column that pushes items upwards. Throw items through the sign at the bottom – signs keep the water in but let items pass. At the top, flowing water carries them over a hopper into the chest. Bubble columns need Minecraft 1.13 or newer.
comparator_fill.name: Fill level display
comparator_fill.desc: A comparator reads how full the chest is (0–15) and sends that strength along a redstone line. The line gets weaker with every block, so the fuller the chest, the more lamps light up (one lamp per two levels). Glowstone between the lamps keeps them from lighting each other.
night_light.name: Night light
night_light.desc: An inverted daylight detector gives a signal at night. The redstone line on top of the lamps switches them on automatically in the dark and off again in the morning. Right-click the detector to invert it.
